text.p: Ethiopia on Thursday appointed Tefera Walewa as deputy prime minister and defence minister, replacing Tamirat Layne who was earlier dismissed as secretary-general of his party for breaches of discipline.
State-run Ethiopian News Agency (ENA) said the Ethiopian parliament, sitting in an extraordinary session, approved the appointment of Tefera, who was nominated by Prime Minister Meles Zenawi.

The Amhara National Democratic Movement (ANDM), a coalition partner of the ruling Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF), said in a statement that Tamirat had behaved contrary to the discipline of his party and no longer represented ANDM in any capacity.

"It is the strong conviction of the central committee of the ANDM that there are no grounds for Ato Tamirat, who failed to discipline himself, to discharge his responsibilites to continue with the high post in the government and as the representative of the movement in parliament", it said.
ANDM gave no further details of the disciplinary breaches.
Tefera, who is a founding member of the ANDM and a member of the executive committee of the EPDRF was the administrator of the capital, Addis Ababa, before his new appointment.
